D.t: Rob Sand leads by 5.5 in the forecast and wins 85% of simulations. The cushion is about 75,639 votes; a one point swing is about 6,864 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +1.5 and D +12.7. A normal polling error decides it.

The polls page average is D +6.4. Your best recent poll is Cook Political Report/GS Strategy Group and New River Strategies at D +11.0; your worst is Echelon Insights for NetChoice at D +3.7. 14 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Polk, a projected net 58,545 votes; Johnson, a projected net 40,356 votes; Linn, a projected net 29,623 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Dallas, D +11.0, 3.6% of the vote; Pottawattamie, D +2.3, 2.5% of the vote; Woodbury, R +4.8, 2.5% of the vote; Warren, D +0.5, 1.9% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Rob Sand runs furthest behind in Sioux, Marion, Dallas. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 92% of voters, 51 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.62 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 73% of voters, 52 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.65 points; Voters without a degree, 64% of voters, 51 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.19 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Rob Sand: Immigration voters 22 to 76, Incomes $125K and up 40 to 58, Small counties 42 to 56. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
Registered Democrats cast 49% of the 338,739 ballots in Iowa so far, against 33% for the other party. That is 8.3 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 1.9 points away from Rob Sand. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
